insights.concise_text: The proposed user-aware encoder-decoder with attention fusion addresses existing approaches' failure to handle personal preference and incomplete recipe details by attending over user profiles learned from previously consumed recipes.

triple.subject: user-aware encoder-decoder with attention fusion
triple.object: personal preference and incomplete recipe details

insights.concise_text: Quantitative perplexity, user-ranking, and qualitative analyses support the claim that personalized models generate high-quality and specific recipes that align with historical user preferences.

triple.subject: Quantitative (perplexity, user-ranking) and qualitative analysis
triple.object: personalized models generate high-quality and specific recipes that align with historical user preferences

insights.concise_text: Because recipe output quality depends on ingredients and cooking techniques, the paper's personalization attends over historical recipe content rather than only user writing styles.

triple.subject: ingredients and cooking techniques
triple.object: personalization to attend over historical recipe content rather than writing styles

insights.concise_text: The released dataset of 180K+ recipes and 700K+ user reviews is the filtered Food.com dataset obtained by discarding users with fewer than 4 reviews.

triple.subject: released dataset of 180K+ recipes and 700K+ user reviews
triple.object: filtered Food.com dataset after discarding users with fewer than 4 reviews

insights.concise_text: The Prior Name model uses averages of name-token embeddings from the k-most recent prior recipes, and it achieves the best UMA and MRR by a large margin.

triple.subject: Prior Name model
triple.object: other personalized models in UMA and MRR

insights.concise_text: The Prior Tech model's technique preference vector is built from techniques seen in R^+_u using the manually constructed list of 58 cooking techniques.

triple.subject: Prior Tech model
triple.object: list of 58 cooking techniques

insights.concise_text: Under sequential leave-one-out evaluation on recipes not in the training set, all personalized models outperform baseline in BPE perplexity, with Prior Name performing the best.

triple.subject: sequential leave-one-out evaluation on recipes not in the training set
triple.object: all personalized models outperform baseline in BPE perplexity

insights.concise_text: The human evaluation used partial recipe specifications with name and 3-5 key ingredients, matching the experimental setting that provides the first 3-5 ingredients listed in each recipe.

triple.subject: human evaluation partial recipe specification
triple.object: first 3-5 ingredients listed in each recipe

insights.concise_text: Human evaluators preferred personalized model outputs to baseline 63% of the time in comparisons where one recipe came from the baseline encoder-decoder model and one from Prior Tech, Prior Name, or Prior Recipe.

triple.subject: personalized model outputs
triple.object: baseline encoder-decoder model in 63% of human preferences

insights.concise_text: The conclusion that personalized generative models produce coherent recipes preferred by human evaluators is supported by recipe-level coherence scores of 1.78-1.82 surpassing the baseline at 1.77 and 63% human preference.

triple.subject: recipe-level coherence scores of 1.78-1.82 and 63% human preference
triple.object: personalized generative models produce coherent recipes preferred by human evaluators
